hypothesis: The parent's only systematic query inefficiency is the model taking a low-information query (~0.29 of best entropy) as its 2nd query on NOT inventories, which are also the long tail toward the 18-query budget. Suggesting only near-best queries (>=0.97 of max entropy) and vetoing proposals below 0.9 of max lowers queries/episode on NOT inventories without lowering final-table accuracy; falsified if NOT-inventory query counts do not drop on average over repeated runs, or if exact accuracy drops below the parent's.
behavior_changes: Suggested-query list is filtered to entries with entropy >= 0.97 x the best (still at most 4, at least 1).
A model-proposed informative query with entropy < 0.9 x the best is vetoed and re-asked with a note naming the suggested queries, the same way as an already-answered or already-implied query.
If all 4 asks in a turn are vetoed, the harness sends the most informative query the model itself proposed, so a stubborn model can't stall the episode (the model still writes every query).
preserved_behaviors: Rule-derived joint enumeration (inventory splits x per-circuit tables) and joint-entropy ranking, unchanged.
Compact per-turn state, veto of answered/implied queries, early stop when every circuit is determined.
Final step: candidate tables listed most-likely-first, per-circuit line parsing, snapping to the nearest consistent candidate.
Frozen solver (self.llm only) and label-free (env.query only); no inventory/index branching.
verification: Audit of the parent: replayed all 20 parent episodes (b0+b1) through its own scorer. Every query was at about the max entropy, except the 2nd query on 7 of 8 NOT=1 episodes (0.29 of max, e.g. i209 A(0,0,0) while B(0,0,1) was suggested). No episode ended with an ambiguous circuit; parent was 10/10 exact on b1 and b0.

Only one branch has traces on b1, so there were no same-instance disagreements between branches to settle. Cross-branch evidence from b0: the b0r0g0/b0r0g1/b0r1g1 lineages (no rule-derived bookkeeping) were 0-2/3 per instance or timed out, so the enumeration and bookkeeping are the independently supported strengths and were kept as-is.

Offline simulation (sampled truths over the joint space; model takes a top-4 suggestion, or any allowed query with p=0.15; 250 episodes per inventory): mean queries 12.25->12.04 (3 AND/3 OR/1 NOT), 12.51->12.15 (1 AND/5 OR/2 NOT), 16.01->15.53 (2 AND/4 OR/3 NOT, hypothetical); episodes over 18 queries 5/250->0/250 on that last inventory.

Ran check_b1r0_cand_pilot_labeled_b10g3r2_b1r0g2.py: 10/10 status ok, final guess parsed, final table correct 10/10, circuits right 3/3 everywhere, 0 crashes. Mean queries 9.9 (parent 10.5). NOT=1 instances: 209 16->14, 236 14->11, 253 15->12, 228 7->12 (the last is worse: different answers led down a different query path).

Read the check results: the veto fired 5 times, only on NOT=1 instances (4 at query 2); the model's re-ask reply was a suggested query every time (B(0,0,1) x4, A(0,1,0) x1); the fallback path never ran.
risks: Single 10-instance run: the 0.6 queries/episode gain is within sampling noise for one run (228 went 7->12); the support for it is mainly the offline simulation.
Extra model calls on vetoed turns (+1-3 calls per NOT episode).
Greedy one-step entropy is still myopic; the veto forces the model even closer to it, so any systematic weakness of greedy now applies more fully.
Fallback path (all 4 asks vetoed) is untested live; it sends a model-written query but one below the floor.
